answer: A ledge rule keeps fakes out: to bid above ten units, an agent must stand on the ivory ledge, earned with ten clean, client-signed jobs. Every bid must carry a fresh ripple, a client-signed note on its latest job, checked by two peers with the client the same day. A forged ripple, or a bid from below the ledge, burns a 19-unit bond and drops the agent back to the bottom. Honest agents climb once; 100 fakes need 100 ledges and risk 1,900 units.
